## Who it is for

Python for Beginners: Economics & Social Sciences is a free, self-paced course by Ning Zhang for students and researchers in economics, sociology, political science, public policy and related fields. You can start with no programming experience.

The first lessons run in Google Colab, a service that runs Python notebooks in your browser. Local installation is an optional later path. The planned statistics sequence ends with ordinary least squares (OLS) and fixed effects. OLS fits a linear relationship; fixed effects account for group-specific differences that stay constant over time. Neither method by itself establishes causation.

## Status and scope

The core path is available: 17 lessons across Parts 0–2 cover the browser notebook, Python basics and pandas data handling. The [course map](lessons/index.qmd) lists each lesson in order. Parts 3–6—visualization, regression, reproducible workflow and projects—remain coming soon. This is a course in development, not a finished release.

## Data and rights

The country panel is an historical teaching extract from Gapminder, packaged by Jennifer Bryan under **CC0**. It covers 142 countries at five-year intervals from 1952 to 2007. It is not current statistics or a complete sample of the world. [Data and attribution details](https://github.com/ningzhanglab/Python-for-Beginners/blob/main/data/README.md) document the exact source and transformations.

Lesson 2.4 uses 120 simulated survey records generated by a committed, fixed-seed script. They contain no actual people. Their deliberately messy responses teach missing values and category cleaning; their wage relationships are built into the simulation, not discovered facts. The dates lesson derives a Canadian time series from the same historical country panel, with observations every five years.

**Course licensing is undecided.** The owner has not yet granted an open license for the course's original code, lesson text or figures. The third-party dataset retains its own CC0 terms. Free access to read a course does not itself grant permission to redistribute its original materials.

## Cite and improve

Suggested informal citation: Ning Zhang. *Python for Beginners: Economics & Social Sciences*. Course in development, 2026. Include the repository URL and the date or commit you used. A versioned release citation will follow a first release.

Use [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/ningzhanglab/Python-for-Beginners/issues) to report an unclear explanation or a broken example. Include the lesson title, what you expected and what happened. Never include student records, passwords or private research data.
